title: Frame and resolve a composition
instructions: Improve the introduction and ending of the charity-sale composition. The response explains how a step-by-step method learned through school projects helped the writer organise the sale and adapt safely when rain disrupted it. Answer all six questions before viewing feedback.

parts.prompt: Which opening enters the task most directly while establishing a usable direction for the response?

options.text: Since the beginning of time, education has always been extremely important to every person in the whole world.
Have you ever wondered what school teaches us? In this essay, I will tell you about something that I learned.

School projects taught me that a large problem becomes manageable when it is divided into clear next actions. I later relied on that method while organising a charity sale, especially when sudden rain forced our team to change plans.
The drinks order was late, the posters were orange, water reached the extension lead, six tables were moved and the hall doors were narrow.

choice_rationales.A: The sweeping claim delays the actual response and cannot be supported by this composition.
choice_rationales.B: The rhetorical question and essay announcement occupy space without identifying the lesson or direction.
choice_rationales.C: The opening answers the task, names the transferable method and points towards the planning and adaptation developed in the body.
choice_rationales.D: The list rushes body evidence before the reader knows the central lesson or organising direction.

parts.hint: Choose the opening that identifies both the learned method and the later situation without giving away every detail.
parts.correct_explanation: The strongest opening provides immediate orientation and a focused route through the response.

parts.prompt: Which THREE jobs should this introduction perform?

options.text: Identify the transferable lesson about clear next actions.
Locate the later charity-sale experience.
Establish that the response will develop planning and adaptation.
List every event and object that will appear in the body.
Define education using a dictionary-style sentence.

choice_rationales.A: The central lesson answers the task and controls the response.
choice_rationales.B: The experience gives the reader enough context for the application of that lesson.
choice_rationales.C: A clear direction prepares the two main stages without mechanically listing paragraphs.
choice_rationales.D: Specific events belong in body paragraphs where their significance can be explained.
choice_rationales.E: A broad definition delays the candidate's own answer and adds no useful direction.

parts.hint: Select the minimum information needed to answer the task and prepare the route through the body.
parts.correct_explanation: A focused introduction identifies the lesson, locates its application and establishes the response's direction.

parts.prompt: Which sentence narrows an overpromised introduction so that it matches the actual body paragraphs?

options.text: The sale taught me everything about leadership, technology, friendship, finance, confidence and the future.
Many useful lessons exist, and all of them are equally important in every situation.
This essay will contain two body paragraphs followed by a conclusion.
The experience showed how breaking work into clear next actions supported both preparation and calm adaptation.

choice_rationales.A: The body cannot develop this long and exaggerated list of claims.
choice_rationales.B: The generalisation removes the specific focus rather than narrowing it.
choice_rationales.C: Announcing the document structure does not establish a meaningful direction.
choice_rationales.D: The sentence promises only the two ideas the body actually develops.

parts.hint: Match the promise to the existing paragraphs about preparation and adaptation.
parts.correct_explanation: A fulfilled narrow promise gives the composition stronger unity than an impressive but unsupported roadmap.

parts.prompt: Which ending resolves the response instead of merely replaying it?

options.text: In conclusion, I learned a step-by-step method at school, used it for a charity sale and dealt with the rain.
The sale showed me that planning is not the same as predicting every problem. Its real value is giving people a clear next action when circumstances change.
After the rain stopped, I also designed a new payment application that doubled the school's donations the following year.
Therefore, everyone in the world should always work hard and never give up on anything.

choice_rationales.A: The sentence compresses earlier content but does not deepen or resolve its significance.
choice_rationales.B: The ending returns to the method after the evidence and states a more precise insight about adaptation.
choice_rationales.C: The new achievement would require evidence and development in another body paragraph.
choice_rationales.D: The generic moral is much broader than the evidence and controlling focus.

parts.hint: Choose the ending that shows what the experience revealed about the central method.
parts.correct_explanation: Resolution returns to the focus at a deeper level: the method matters because it supports action when plans change.

parts.prompt: Which ending contains new evidence that should not appear for the first time in the conclusion?

options.text: The experience changed my view of planning: a plan can guide adaptation without controlling every event.
Clear next actions made the work manageable before the disruption and useful during it.
I now use the same principle whenever a complicated task begins to feel unmanageable.
Six months later, I used a spreadsheet system to organise a regional competition for 300 participants and won an award.

choice_rationales.A: This interprets evidence already developed in the response.
choice_rationales.B: This synthesises the two established applications without inventing another episode.
choice_rationales.C: This states a restrained continuing consequence of the central lesson.
choice_rationales.D: The later competition, exact scale and award are a new episode requiring their own explanation and evidence.

parts.hint: Find the option that opens a new story rather than resolving the existing charity-sale experience.
parts.correct_explanation: A conclusion should close the established reasoning; substantial new evidence belongs in the body.

parts.prompt: Which opening-and-ending pair creates the strongest conceptual closure?

options.text: Opening: ‘School is important.’ Ending: ‘In conclusion, school is important.’

Opening: ‘Can one simple classroom method remain useful when a real plan fails?’ Ending: ‘The rain answered that question: clear next actions did not prevent disruption, but they gave the team a safe way through it.’
Opening: ‘I will discuss planning.’ Ending: ‘Teamwork is the greatest value in the universe.’
Opening: ‘The extension lead was wet.’ Ending: ‘The drinks supplier had arrived before lunch.’

choice_rationales.A: The ending repeats the opening without development.
choice_rationales.B: The ending answers the opening after the evidence and refines the original idea rather than copying it.
choice_rationales.C: The ending shifts to an exaggerated focus that the opening did not establish.
choice_rationales.D: The two details do not frame a central idea or show what the response has established.

parts.hint: Look for a final sentence that answers or deepens the direction established at the start.
parts.correct_explanation: The matched pair creates closure by moving from a genuine opening question to a precise evidence-based answer.
